questions.question: Which is NOT correct about the President of India?
questions.option_1: He has veto power by which he can withhold or refuse to give assent to Bills including Money Bill passed by the Parliament.
questions.option_2: Every bill passed by the Parliament goes to the President for his assent before it becomes a law.
questions.option_3: The President holds office for a period of five years.
questions.option_4: He is a part of the Parliament.
questions.solution: The statement that the President 'can withhold or refuse to give assent to... Money Bill' is NOT correct. While the President has veto power over ordinary bills, they are generally expected to give assent to a Money Bill because it is introduced in the Parliament only with their prior recommendation. Facts: The President is indeed a part of the Parliament (Art 79) and holds office for five years.

questions.question: Which of the following directs the State to provide ‘Equal justice and free legal aid’?
questions.option_1: Part V of the Indian Constitution
questions.option_2: Part VII of the Indian Constitution
questions.option_3: Part IV of the Indian Constitution
questions.option_4: Part VI of the Indian Constitution
questions.solution: Part IV of the Indian Constitution, which contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP), directs the State to provide 'Equal justice and free legal aid' under Article 39A. This article was added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976, to ensure that justice is not denied to any citizen due to economic or other disabilities.

questions.question: Which of following Articles of the Constitution, gives the right to consult a legal practitioner of one's choice?
questions.solution: Article 22 of the Constitution provides the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of one's choice. This is part of the protection against arrest and detention in certain cases. It ensures that any person who is arrested is informed of the grounds for such arrest as soon as possible.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles establishes the provision of the Right to Education?
questions.solution: Article 21A establishes the Right to Education. It declares that the State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years. This was inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.

questions.question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution is known as ‘Magna Carta of India’?
questions.solution: Part III (Fundamental Rights) is known as the ‘Magna Carta of India’. It contains a very comprehensive and long list of justiciable Fundamental Rights. It is inspired by the US Constitution's Bill of Rights and the historical English Magna Carta of 1215.

questions.question: Who among the following holds the authority of transferring judges from one High Court to another after consulting with the Chief Justice of India?
questions.solution: The President of India holds the authority to transfer judges from one High Court to another. According to Article 222, this power is exercised after consultation with the Chief Justice of India (CJI). In practice, this follows the 'Collegium' system recommendations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT correct about the power of the Speaker of the state Legislative Assembly?
questions.option_1: He adjourns the Assembly or suspends the meeting in the absence of a quorum.
questions.option_2: He decides whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not.
questions.option_3: He maintains order and decorum of the House.
questions.option_4: He calls for a joint session of the Assembly and Council to resolve the deadlock between the two Houses over an ordinary Bill.
questions.solution: The statement that the Speaker 'calls for a joint session' is NOT correct. In the case of a deadlock in a State Legislature (between the Assembly and the Council), there is no provision for a joint sitting. Note: Joint sittings (Article 108) only exist at the Central level (Parliament) and are summoned by the President, not the Speaker.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a national political party?
questions.solution: The National Conference (NC) is a regional/state party primarily active in Jammu and Kashmir, NOT a national political party. National Parties: As of the 2024 context, major national parties include the BJP, INC, AAP, and BSP. The Nationalist Congress Party (NCP) recently lost its national status in some technical classifications, but it was historically one.

questions.question: As of 15th March 2021, how many women judges are there in the Supreme Court of India?
questions.solution: As of the specified period (including the expansion in late 2021), the Supreme Court saw a historic rise in representation, reaching 4 women judges simultaneously (Justices Indira Banerjee, Hima Kohli, B.V. Nagarathna, and Bela M. Trivedi). Milestone: Justice B.V. Nagarathna is in line to become the first female Chief Justice of India in 2027.

questions.question: The emoluments and allowances of the President and other expenditure relating to his office is charged on the ______ of India.
questions.solution: The emoluments and allowances of the President are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India. Significance: 'Charged' expenditure means these amounts are not subject to the annual vote of Parliament, ensuring the financial independence and dignity of the highest constitutional office.

questions.question: In which of the following Articles, is it mentioned that Directive Principles are NOT justiciable?
questions.solution: Article 37 explicitly mentions that the Directive Principles are NOT justiciable by any court. However, it also states that these principles are fundamental in the governance of the country, and it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for the power to the President to convene a joint sitting of the both the Houses of Parliament?
questions.solution: Article 108 of the Constitution provides for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament. It is summoned by the President and presided over by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha. This mechanism is used to resolve a deadlock between the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha over an ordinary bill.

questions.question: The last Sub-Section (k) on the education of children was added in 2002 as a part of the Fundamental Duties. The same Amendment also introduced _________ in the Constitution.
questions.solution: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002, which added the fundamental duty sub-section (k), also introduced Article 21A (Right to Education) as a Fundamental Right. It also changed the subject matter of Article 45 in the Directive Principles regarding early childhood care.

questions.question: The Fundamental Duties are addressed to the ________.
questions.solution: The Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) are specifically addressed to the Citizens of India. Unlike Fundamental Rights, which are primarily enforceable against the State, these duties serve as a reminder to citizens of their social and moral obligations to the nation.

questions.question: Fundamental Duties have ____________, social and economic significance.
questions.solution: Fundamental Duties have ethical, social, and economic significance. They act as a code of conduct or moral integration for the citizens, encouraging them to maintain discipline and commitment toward the country's progress and harmony.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution states ‘No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to a procedure established by law’?
questions.solution: Article 21 states: 'No person shall be deprived of his life or personal liberty except according to a procedure established by law.' This is considered the most evolved and important article in the Constitution, as the Supreme Court has interpreted it to include the right to privacy, clean environment, and livelihood.

questions.question: In India, the judicial system is largely autonomous. The Judiciary must use its powers under Articles 32 and ____________ to protect the fundamental rights given in the Constitution of India.
questions.solution: The Judiciary must use its powers under Article 32 (Supreme Court) and Article 13 to protect Fundamental Rights. Article 13 is crucial because it gives the courts the power of Judicial Review, allowing them to declare any law void if it is inconsistent with Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India deals with the Conduct of Business of the Government of a State?
questions.solution: Article 166 deals with the Conduct of Business of the Government of a State. it specifies that all executive actions of the Government of a State shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the Governor and outlines how orders and instruments are to be authenticated.

questions.question: Which feature of the Constitution of India is borrowed from Japan?
questions.option_1: The procedure is established by law
questions.option_4: Impeachment of President and Supreme Court Judges
questions.solution: The feature 'Procedure established by law' was borrowed from the Constitution of Japan. Others: Amendment of Constitution is from South Africa, Prerogative writs and Parliamentary system are from Britain, and Impeachment is from the US.

questions.question: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:
questions.option_1: Both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
questions.solution: The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha (the House of the People), as per Article 75(3). This means the ministry stays in power only as long as it enjoys the confidence of the majority in the lower house.

questions.question: Which of the following is called as ‘the temple of the country’s democracy’?
questions.solution: The Parliament of India is often referred to as the 'temple of the country’s democracy'. It is the supreme legislative body of the Republic of India and represents the sovereign will of the people through their elected representatives.
